html:
The great Gothic brick church of the Franciscan friars in Venice, in the San Polo district. The city gave the friars land here in 1231. Their first church, begun in 1250 and finished in 1338, was already too small, and work began almost at once on the present church, which took more than a century: the bell tower, the second tallest in Venice, was done in 1396, the façade in 1440, and the church was consecrated in 1492.

Like many Franciscan churches it is plain outside, red brick with details in white Istrian stone. Inside, a tall ribbed vault covers the nave, which leads through the only choir screen still in place in Venice (1475) to the high altar. There Titian's Assumption of the Virgin, painted from 1515 to 1518, hangs where it was made to hang. It is the largest altarpiece in the city, and its gesturing apostles broke with the calm of earlier Venetian painting. Titian also painted the Pesaro Madonna for the Pesaro family's altar, and the chapels hold a triptych by Giovanni Bellini and a Saint John the Baptist by Donatello.

The church is full of tombs, among them those of the doges Francesco Foscari and Nicolò Tron. Titian, who died in 1576, is buried here, and so is the composer Claudio Monteverdi. The monument to Antonio Canova holds only his heart; it follows Canova's own design for a tomb for Titian that was never built.
